note: Submodule of Toc.js. Provides a text-format filter plugin toc_js_filter (title 'TOC.js shortcode: [toc]') that replaces [toc] in text with a Toc.js table of contents; settings mirror the Toc.js block settings (schema filter_settings.toc_js_filter). Enable it on a text format (filter.format.<id> -> filters.toc_js_filter.status: true). Requires toc_js. No settings page/configure route/permissions/Drush. Introspection reads which format has the filter and its settings; execution enables the filter on a format and creates a format with the filter. Uses namespaced text formats (tocjsf_*), no node operations (safe on this shared site).

evals.prompt: What token does the toc_js_filter module let editors put in body text, and what is it replaced with? What is the filter plugin id?
evals.expected_output: The filter (plugin id toc_js_filter, 'TOC.js shortcode: [toc]') replaces the [toc] token in text with a rendered Toc.js table of contents.

evals.prompt: How do I turn on the Toc.js [toc] shortcode so it works in my content?
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'TOC.js shortcode: [toc]' filter (toc_js_filter) on the text format(s) you use (e.g. Full HTML) at Administration > Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors, then configure its settings. Any [toc] in a field using that format renders a TOC.

evals.prompt: What settings does the toc_js_filter [toc] filter offer, and where does the table of contents markup actually get generated?
evals.expected_output: Its settings form reuses the Toc.js settings (TocJsService::getTocForm) — selectors, container, list type, smooth scrolling, back-to-top, etc. — stored under schema filter_settings.toc_js_filter. The TOC list itself is still generated client-side by the toc.js library; the filter injects an empty .toc-js container where [toc] was.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one text format has the Toc.js [toc] filter (toc_js_filter) enabled. Inspect the live text formats and give the machine name (format id) of that format.
evals.expected_output: The text format tocjsf_intro has filters.toc_js_filter.status = true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the text format tocjsf_sel has the Toc.js [toc] filter enabled with custom heading selectors. Inspect the live filter configuration and state the selectors value.
On this Drupal site there is a text format tocjsf_build that does not yet have the Toc.js [toc] filter. Enable the toc_js_filter filter on that format and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the filter: $format = FilterFormat::load('tocjsf_build'); $format->setFilterConfig('toc_js_filter', ['status'=>TRUE,'weight'=>0,'settings'=>[]]); $format->save(); so filter.format.tocjsf_build filters.toc_js_filter.status is true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a new text format with machine name tocjsf_new that has the Toc.js [toc] filter (toc_js_filter) enabled, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a FilterFormat 'tocjsf_new' and enable toc_js_filter on it (setFilterConfig with status TRUE), then save, so filter.format.tocjsf_new filters.toc_js_filter.status is true.
